html:
SMTO-SKL-0084 — The dates or times for this calendar request don't work

GUID: da2e9307-a108-5903-8b13-69db2f4514f1
Slug: microsoft365-invalid-time-range
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't turn the dates and times into a clear time period, for example because the end is before the start, the time zone is missing, or the time is skipped when clocks change. Nothing was created or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. State the start, the end and the time zone together, for example “December 3, 2 PM to 3 PM, New York time”. SMTO needs all three to know the exact moment you mean.
  2. Make sure the end comes after the start, and keep calendar searches to under a year, or under 62 days when checking free and busy times. SMTO and Microsoft only accept time periods that move forward and stay within these lengths.
  3. If the time falls on the night the clocks change, pick a time outside that hour. That hour is skipped or happens twice, so the time is unclear.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the events or creates the event at the time you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the dates and time zone you used, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 calendar time validation failed: a date/time could not be parsed, start/end/timezone were not supplied together, a local time fell in a DST gap or an ambiguous repeated hour without a matching offset, a recurring boundary hit a DST fold, or the window was not increasing or exceeded its limit (366 days; under 62 days for availability).

What this means

  • Date/time parsing, DST disambiguation, required start/end/timezone fields, recurrence fold handling or the operation's increasing bounded window fails validation. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Date/time parsing, DST disambiguation, required start/end/timezone fields, recurrence fold handling or the operation's increasing bounded window fails validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect offsets, timezone, start/end ordering and operation-specific duration bounds.

How to fix it

  • Supply start, end and timezone together as ISO 8601 values with end strictly after start, within 366 days (under 62 days for calendar_availability). Correct nonexistent local times in DST gaps, add the explicit UTC offset for repeated fall-back times, and move recurring events off a DST fold.
  • Provide an increasing bounded time window with an explicit timezone. DST folds require a matching offset; nonexistent local times must be corrected.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended interval is explicit, increasing and valid across DST rules.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
